latest_release.name: Hanko v3.2
latest_release.body:
Hanko v3.2 brings important vulnerability fixes, adds lifecycle management for SAML certificates and improves the reliability of SAML sign-in. This release also tightens redirect URL validation, improves passkey registration in the frontend SDK, and adds Danish translations.

## Security

This release fixes the following security vulnerabilities. We recommend all users upgrade to 3.2.0.

- Deleting a SAML provider in a multi-tenant setup deleted the linked social, OIDC and SAML identities of all users in all tenants, not just the ones tied to that provider. [GHSA-9c6x-m5j7-cj8h](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/security/advisories/GHSA-9c6x-m5j7-cj8h)                                                
- The SAML redirect allowlist matched wildcard entries without checking where the host ends, so `https://app.example.com**` also accepted `https://app.example.com.evil.com`. This could leak a one-time login token to an attacker's domain and lead to account takeover. [GHSA-jfqc-fr2q-fvx6](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/security/advisories/GHSA-jfqc-fr2q-fvx6)
- The one-time nonce for SP-initiated SAML logins could be used more than once at the same time, so a captured SAML response could produce extra login tokens. [GHSA-q5g6-55h6-gm58](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/security/advisories/GHSA-q5g6-55h6-gm58)
- A disabled SAML identity provider could still be used for IdP-initiated login. [GHSA-pm29-79w6-73xj](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/security/advisories/GHSA-pm29-79w6-73xj)
- A captured IdP-initiated SAML assertion could be replayed by changing the unsigned Response ID, when the IdP signs only the assertions and not the response. [GHSA-5q99-9mgg-pcwh](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/security/advisories/GHSA-5q99-9mgg-pcwh)
- Two login flows running at the same time could both accept the same TOTP code, which broke the rule that each code works only once. [GHSA-h4w8-v289-cr8w](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/security/advisories/GHSA-h4w8-v289-cr8w)

## SAML certificate lifecycle

Hanko now supports managing the lifecycle of SAML certificates, helping teams prepare for certificate changes before they affect sign-in. Hanko also signs SAML authentication requests sent via HTTP Redirect, records SAML callback failures correctly in the audit log, and fixes SAML lookups on MySQL.

See [#3038](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/3038), [#3042](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/3042), [#3068](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/3068), and [#3062](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/3062).

## Redirect URL validation

Third-party sign-in now rejects wildcard-only entries in `allowed_redirect_urls`. Hanko also validates each entry in the SAML redirect allowlist. If your third-party sign-in configuration uses a standalone `*`, replace it with the redirect URLs your application needs before upgrading.

See [#2999](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/2999) and [#3091](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/3091).

## More improvements

- **Passkey registration:** The frontend SDK now enforces a deadline for passkey creation so the registration flow can recover if the ceremony does not complete. See [#2883](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/2883).
- **Danish translations:** Hanko Elements and authentication emails are now available in Danish. See [#2992](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/2992).
- **Tenant-aware security notifications:** Security notifications now use the configuration of the tenant they belong to. See [#3162](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/3162).
- **Audit logs:** `actor_user_id` now contains the public user ID, making it easier to match audit events to users through the API. See [#3037](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/pull/3037).

Thanks to everyone who contributed to this release!

detail.readme: --- [![Test Status](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/actions/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml/badge.svg)](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/actions/workflows/codeql-analysis.yml) [![Build Status](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/workflows/Go/badge.svg)](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/actions/workflows/go.yml) [![GoDoc](https://godoc.org/github.com/teamhanko/hanko?status.svg)](https://godoc.org/github.com/teamhanko/hanko) [![npm (scoped)](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@teamhanko/hanko-elements?label=hanko-elements)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@teamhanko/hanko-elements) [![npm (scoped)](https://img.shields.io/npm/v/@teamhanko/hanko-frontend-sdk?label=hanko-frontend-sdk)](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@teamhanko/hanko-frontend-sdk) # About Hanko Hanko is an open source authentication and user management solution that is easy to integrate, framework-agnostic, and built on privacy-first principles like data minimalism and phishing resistance. - Supports all modern authentication methods: passwords, MFA, passkeys, social logins, and SAML SSO - Flexible configuration options, including passkey-only, OAuth-only, and user-deletable passwords - Easy integration with **Hanko Elements** web components - A robust API that handles all authentication and onboarding flow states, enabling fast, reliable custom frontend implementations - API-first, lightweight, cloud-native Available for self-hosting and as a fully managed service on [Hanko Cloud](https://www.hanko.io). # Features To follow the development of this project, watch our releases, leave a star, sign up to our [Product News](https://www.hanko.io/updates) or join our [Discord Community](https://www.hanko.io/community). Here's a brief overview of Hanko's current and upcoming features: | Status | Feature | |:------:| :--- | |✅| Email / username identifiers | |✅| Passwords, passcodes, passkeys | |✅| Hanko Elements web components | |✅| OAuth SSO (Sign in with Apple/Google/GitHub and more) | |✅| i18n & custom translations | |✅| SAML Enterprise SSO | |✅| Webhooks | |✅| Server-side sessions & remote session revocation | |✅| MFA (TOTP, security keys) | |✅| Custom OIDC/OAuth connections | |✅| JS SDK | |⚙️| Organizations, Roles, Permissions | | | `` web component | | | iOS, Android, React Native, Flutter SDKs | Visit our [Roadmap](https://www.hanko.io/roadmap) for more information on upcoming features. # Contact us Schedule a demo with the team. Learn how you can built state-of-the-art authentication for your apps effortlessly with Hanko. # Architecture The main building blocks of the Hanko project are - [backend](/backend/README.md) - Scalable, robust, and lightweight authentication API for passwords, passkeys, email passcodes, OAuth SSO, user and session management, and JWT issuing - [hanko-elements](/frontend/elements/README.md) - Web components made for the Hanko API that provide onboarding, login, and user profile functionality and are customizable with CSS - [hanko-frontend-sdk](/frontend/frontend-sdk/README.md) - A client package for using the Hanko API The remainder of the repository consists of: - [quickstart](/quickstart) - A quickstart example app showing off Hanko's login experience and acting as a reference implementation - [examples](frontend/examples) - Example implementations for a number of frameworks - docs - The Hanko documentation ([docs.hanko.io](https://docs.hanko.io)) -> Moved to its own repo here: https://github.com/teamhanko/docs # Getting started 1. Try our hosted [live example](https://example.hanko.io) and our companion page [passkeys.io](https://www.passkeys.io) or use the [quickstart app](/quickstart/README.md) to get a feel for the user experience provided by an application that leverages the Hanko backend API and our custom web component 2. To run the project locally, there are two options available: - Bare metal: - Head over to the [backend](/backend/README.md) section to learn how to get it up and running for your own project. Use [Hanko Cloud](https://cloud.hanko.io) for a hosted backend. - Docker: - If you prefer to use [Docker](https://www.docker.com/) to run the project locally, please visit the [Run the quickstart](./quickstart/README.md#run-the-quickstart) for information on how to run the project. This will create everything, including frontend and backend components. - If you wish to keep only the backend components, you can modify the [quickstart.yaml](./deploy/docker-compose/quickstart.yaml) to remove the unnecessary services. To make changes to the configuration to meet your needs, modify [config.yaml](./deploy/docker-compose/config.yaml). 3. Then, integrate [hanko-elements](/frontend/elements/README.md) – we provide [example applications](frontend/examples/README.md) and [guides](https://docs.hanko.io/guides/frontend) for your favourite frontend framework in the official documentation If you want to use the Hanko backend API but prefer to build your own UI, you can still make use of the [hanko-frontend-sdk](/frontend/frontend-sdk/README.md). It forms the basis of our web components, and the client it provides handles communication with the [Hanko backend API](https://docs.hanko.io/api-reference/introduction) and saves you the time of rolling your own. # Community ## Questions, bugs, ideas If you have any questions or issues, please check this project's [Q&A section in discussions](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/discussions/categories/q-a) and the [open issues](https://github.com/teamhanko/hanko/issues). Feel free to comment on existing issues or create a new issue if you encounter any bugs or have a feature request. For yet unanswered questions, feedback, or new ideas, please open a new discussion. ## Discord community & X We invite you to join our growing [Discord Community](https://www.hanko.io/community) if you want to get the latest updates on passkeys, WebAuthn, and this project or if you just want to chat with us. You can also [follow us on X](https://x.com/hanko_io). # Licenses [hanko-elements](frontend/elements) and [hanko-frontend-sdk](frontend/frontend-sdk) are licensed under the [MIT License](frontend/elements/LICENSE). Everything else in this repository, including [hanko backend](backend), is licensed under the [AGPL-3.0](/LICENSE). Non-Copyleft commercial licensing is available on request.
